thread.title: Some major changes in holdings occurred at Berkshire Hathawa

author: Mark Bern, CFA
title: Some major changes in holdings occurred at Berkshire Hathawa
text:
Some major changes in holdings occurred at Berkshire Hathaway (NYSE: BRK.A ) (NYSE: BRK.B ) in its investment portfolio over the latest quarter. Today we will expose the changes and rate those purchases and sales with our Friedrich algorithm.
First we need to list all the holdings (excluding those companies that are wholly owned) with increases and decreases made during the fourth quarter of 2017 according to the SEC Form 13-F filing by the company. We compiled the table below from the recent filing and compared it the previous filing to capture the changes. 
Table created by Mark Bern, CFA; Source of data: SEC Form 13-F 
Additions The largest purchase that got all the media coverage was the purchase of about $6B in additional Apple ( AAPL ) shares. That was the largest transaction of the quarter and made Apple its largest holding.
But the addition of Teva Pharmaceutical Industries ( TEVA ) did not get nearly the publicity. Two years ago the stock hit $59 and now sits at $19.80. It must be a value play because the company pays only a 1.77% dividend. The Oracle of Omaha (or his understudies) must believe in the future of generics.

Berkshire also appears to like the financial sector with additional shares having been added to both US Bancorp ( USB ) and The Bank of New York Mellon ( BK ). That makes sense with the expectation of looser regulation for Banks from the Administration. It also makes sense with interest rates on the rise which should allow banks to increase the interest spreads leading to more profitability.
